---
title: "Hua-t’ou"
subtitle: "A Method of Zen Meditation1"
description: |
    <em>Hua-t’ou</em>, literally transalated 'head word' or 'critical phrase' is a practice used in Chinese Chan, Japanese Zen and Korean Seon. This practice is less well known than <em>koans</em>, which are longer, presented with a poetic introduction and an elaborate commentary. A <em>hua-t’ou</em> however is a stand alone, always short phrase that can be taken as a subject of meditation and introspection. The method was revived by the legendary modern Chan Master Xu Yun (1840-1959, pictured). As explained in this paper, it is particularly suited for household practitioners. The paper is taken from <a href=https://buddhistuniversity.net/content/essays/hua-tou_lachs-stuart>the Open Buddhist University</a>.
author: Stuart Lachs
image: /images/master-xu-yun.webp
